claim: On 2025-07-03 the maximum Aurora cluster storage volume doubled from 128 TiB to 256 TiB for Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition. The Aurora features page now gives 256 TiB as the maximum size of the database volume.
question: What is the maximum Aurora cluster storage volume now, and what was it before July 2025?

qualifiers.condition: a cluster must run a supported engine version to use the larger limit; the Aurora size-limits list also gives 256 TiB for Aurora MySQL 3.10 and higher

evidence.quote: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition now supports a maximum storage limit of 256 TiB, doubling the previous limit of 128 TiB.
Your database volume expands in increments of 10 GB up to a maximum of 256 TiB so you never need to provision excess storage in advance.

note: d27-009. Older exam material says 128 TiB. The post names Aurora PostgreSQL; CHAP_Limits lists 256 TiB for PostgreSQL 17.5, 16.9, 15.13 and higher and for MySQL 3.10 and higher.

claim: Since 2024-11-20 Aurora serverless can scale down to 0 ACUs instead of stopping at 0.5 ACUs. To use it you set the minimum capacity to 0 ACUs, and the instance pauses after a period of inactivity.
question: What is the lowest capacity an Aurora serverless instance can scale to now, and what was it before November 2024?

qualifiers.condition: needs a supported engine version (guide: Aurora PostgreSQL 16.3, 15.7, 14.12, 13.15 or higher; Aurora MySQL 3.08.0 or higher)

evidence.quote: Instead of scaling down to 0.5 ACUs, the database can now scale down to 0 ACUs.

| [Aurora serverless supports automatic pause and resume](#WhatsNew) | Aurora serverless DB instances can now scale all the way down to zero Aurora capacity units (ACUs) after a period of inactivity. To enable this feature, you set the minimum capacity value to 0 ACUs. For more information, see [Automatic pause and resume for Aurora serverless](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2-auto-pause.html). | November 20, 2024 |

note: d27-079. Two history rows say Aurora serverless can scale to zero: July 25, 2024 and November 20, 2024. The What's New post and the version table in the guide point to the November 2024 launch as the general one. Older exam material says the minimum is 0.5 ACU. The Aurora pricing page example still says the minimum you can set is 0.5 ACUs, so the pricing example lags the guide.

claim: On 2023-08-21 Aurora added managed Global Database Failover: you can convert a secondary Region into the new primary Region in typically a minute and keep the Global Database configuration. The planned-event operation, earlier called managed planned failover, is now called switchover.
question: What did Aurora add in August 2023 for unplanned Regional outages, and what was managed planned failover renamed to?

qualifiers.condition: unplanned events such as a Regional outage; uses managed failover, not switchover

evidence.quote: With Global Database Failover, you can convert a secondary region into the new primary region in typically a minute and also maintain the multi-region Global Database configuration.
For planned operational procedures such as Regional rotation, use the switchover mechanism (previously called "managed planned failover").

note: d27-050. Old term and the old cross-Region recovery wording: before this, a Regional outage needed a manual failover. Switchover is for planned events and has RPO 0; failover has a non-zero RPO.

claim: Each Aurora global database now has a global database writer endpoint that Aurora updates automatically to point to the current writer instance in the global cluster, so applications need no code or configuration change after a cross-Region failover or switchover.
question: What does the Aurora Global Database writer endpoint do after a failover or switchover?

values.display: automatically updates to point to the current writer instance
values.spoken: updates itself to the current writer

evidence.quote: The new Global Database writer endpoint automatically updates to point to the current writer instance in your global cluster.

The most convenient way to do so is to connect to the Aurora Global Database writer endpoint, which always points to the primary DB cluster, even after a switchover or failover to a different AWS Region.

note: d27-050, d27-141. Before October 2024 applications had to find the new primary after a cross-Region operation.

claim: Aurora PostgreSQL Limitless Database offers distributed query planning and transaction management, so you do not need custom solutions or multiple databases to scale a relational workload beyond a single Aurora writer instance.

values.spoken: distributed query planning and transaction management

qualifiers.condition: general availability announced 2024-10-31; Aurora PostgreSQL only

evidence.quote: Aurora PostgreSQL Limitless Database offers capabilities such as distributed query planning and transaction management, removing the need for you to create custom solutions or manage multiple databases to scale.

note: d27-113. Horizontal write scaling; the decision guide says to use it when a workload needs more write throughput or storage than a single Aurora instance.

claim: All new Aurora DB clusters created on or after February 18, 2026 are encrypted by default with an AWS owned key. Older clusters that did not opt in to encryption stay as they were.
question: Are new Aurora DB clusters encrypted by default, and with which key?

values.display: encrypted by default with an AWS owned key
values.spoken: encrypted by default with an AWS owned key

qualifiers.condition: the What's New post is dated February 16, 2026; the guide gives February 18, 2026

evidence.quote: All new DB clusters created on or after February 18, 2026, are encrypted by default with an AWS owned key.
Aurora now automatically encrypts all new database clusters created without custom encryption settings using server-side encryption by default.

note: Changed recently: before this, Aurora encryption at rest was something you turned on at creation. Security bullet; older exam questions assume 'enable encryption' as a step.

claim: You cannot disable encryption on new Aurora clusters, but you can choose a customer managed key or an AWS managed KMS key instead of server-side encryption when you create the cluster.

qualifiers.condition: applies to new clusters where no encryption configuration is provided

evidence.quote: You cannot disable encryption on new clusters, but can choose customer-managed or AWS-managed KMS keys instead of server side encryption during cluster creation.

note: Changed recently. Same post: existing clusters remain unaffected.

claim: Existing Aurora clusters are not changed by default server-side encryption, and they keep their current encryption configuration with customer managed or AWS managed KMS keys.

evidence.quote: Existing clusters remain unaffected and you can continue using the current encryption configuration with customer-managed or AWS-managed KMS keys.
